strategy.summary: Reproduce GH#32572 in pandas: Index.get_indexer with method pad/backfill/nearest must return -1 for NaT/NaN targets. The developer's tests (datetime, numeric, timedelta indexing tests) should fail on buggy commit 0563919a033e and pass on the fixed revision. Build pandas from source in editable mode, then run the three test files selecting the new tests by name.

system_packages: a C/C++ compiler toolchain (gcc or clang)
pinned_because: NumPy, python-dateutil, tzdata and Cython have no documented constraint and no era table entry in the evidence; versions are unbounded and left to the current pip resolution, so no pin is asserted
Python version is not stated in the evidence, so it is left null rather than invented

strategy.test_command: python -m pytest pandas/tests/indexes/datetimes/test_indexing.py::TestDatetimeIndex -k 'test_get_indexer_nat_target or test_get_indexer_nat_in_target_mixed' pandas/tests/indexes/numeric/test_indexing.py pandas/tests/indexes/timedeltas/test_indexing.py -k 'test_get_indexer_nan_target or test_get_indexer_nat_target' -v
strategy.reproducing_test: pandas/tests/indexes/datetimes/test_indexing.py::test_get_indexer_nat_target (parametrized over tz in [None, US/Central] and method in [pad, backfill, nearest]); pandas/tests/indexes/datetimes/test_indexing.py::test_get_indexer_nat_in_target_mixed; pandas/tests/indexes/numeric/test_indexing.py::test_get_indexer_nan_target (method parametrized); pandas/tests/indexes/timedeltas/test_indexing.py::test_get_indexer_nat_target (method parametrized)
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 0563919a033e the new tests fail: searchsorted(...)-1 yields a valid index instead of -1 for pad, so tm.assert_numpy_array_equal against expected [-1] (or [-1,2,-1] for the mixed case) raises AssertionError. On the fixed revision the same tests pass, because _get_indexer masks NaT/NaN target entries to -1 when method is not None and target._can_hold_na and not target._is_multi.
strategy.numerical_probe: Compare dti.get_indexer(DatetimeIndex([pd.NaT], dtype=dti.dtype), method='pad') against np.array([-1], dtype=np.intp) for tz None and US/Central.

input_output_examples.expected_output: -1 (NaT must not map to a valid index)

risks: The dtype-specific defect is not confirmed for one dtype: NaN is shown on float64 Index, NaT on datetime64 and timedelta64, and the tz-aware mismatch only as datetime64[ns, tz] vs datetime64[ns]. The tests cover all three, but the tz-aware get_loc path from issue #32572 is not directly exercised by the listed tests, so the traceback case may not transition through these tests.
The buggy and fixed behaviour is described as platform-independent, but no architecture or sanitiser requirement is stated; none is assumed here.
Signed zero, infinities and subnormals are not mentioned, so no probe for them is planned.
The 1301 and 0 outputs come from the issue report and are not confirmed as exact values in the test suite; expected values in the tests are used instead.
Build requires a compiler toolchain; a build failure would prevent any transition from being observed.
PR date is not given, so the exact revision of the fixed commit cannot be checked against the date.
Mixed NaT/real target values in the PR body have no numeric values beyond the test expectation [-1,2,-1].

oracle.reference_source: Expected arrays in the developer's tests (np.array([-1], dtype=np.intp) and np.array([-1,2,-1], dtype=np.intp)) compared with tm.assert_numpy_array_equal.
oracle.why: get_indexer returns integer positions, so exact integer equality is the correct check; no tolerance applies.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On buggy 0563919a033e, pad/backfill/nearest on a NaT or NaN target return a valid position instead of -1 because searchsorted places NaT at the end; tm.assert_numpy_array_equal raises AssertionError against expected [-1].
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision the _get_indexer mask sets NaT/NaN target entries to -1, so the arrays match exactly and the tests pass.
